The Hebrew says “Thus let him curse”; BSB frames the clause as “If he curses me.”
The Hebrew says “who came out from my inward parts”; BSB renders this as “my own flesh and blood.”
The Hebrew names “my eye” and repeats the LORD’s name; BSB has “my affliction” and leaves the second LORD implicit.

The Hebrew explicitly names Hushai in the speech formula and calls Absalom by name twice; BSB uses pronouns instead.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Hushai and Absalom; BSB names only Hushai.
The Hebrew says “before his son” and “I will be before you”; BSB condenses the first and renders the second as serving.
The Hebrew command is plural and explicitly says “for yourselves”; BSB says “Give me counsel.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Ahithophel and Absalom and says “house”; BSB leaves the addressee implicit and uses “palace.”
The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats “the counsel of Ahithophel”; BSB rearranges the second clause as the regard David and Absalom had for it.
